rules.statement: Single-session logout (RP-Initiated or Back-Channel) must revoke only the grants issued under the terminating session, filtered by its `sid`, and fall back to subject-wide revocation only when no session can be resolved.
rules.why: Revoking every grant the subject holds over-revokes: signing out on one device would invalidate the refresh tokens of the subject's other concurrent sessions, which is not correct single-logout behavior.
rules.check: Look for logout or end-session handlers that call grant revocation filtered only by subject (or subject and client) even when a session id is available, or that skip the session-scoped path.

rules.statement: Make "sign out everywhere" (subject-wide grant revocation) an explicit, separate administrative operation, never a side effect of ending one session.
rules.why: Global sign-out is a deliberate action. If it happens as part of single logout, the subject's other sessions are silently killed.
rules.check: Look for subject-wide revocation added to session logout flows as the default behavior instead of only as the no-session fallback.

rules.statement: Every grant issued under an authenticated interactive session (authorization codes, refresh tokens, per-access-token claims grants, and the session grant itself) must have the session's `sid` stamped on it at issuance, and non-interactive grants must store null.
rules.why: Session-scoped revocation can only find grants that carry the sid. A session-bound grant left with null keeps its tokens alive after the session ends.
rules.check: In new or changed grant-issuance paths that run under a user session, check that the session id from the authenticated subject is set on the persisted grant. Flag session-bound grant types that leave it null.

rules.statement: Revoking a session must revoke the session grant together with every child grant and token minted under it, through one complete revocation path rather than a separate partial one.
rules.why: A path that revokes only the session record leaves its child tokens live. A single session-scoped revocation is both complete and the one path to maintain.
rules.check: Look for session-revocation methods that delete or revoke only the session entry without revoking the grants carrying its sid, or a second redundant revocation API for the same purpose.

rules.statement: Index and match opaque, case-significant identifiers (such as a Base64Url `sid`) verbatim, without adding a normalized companion column or case-folding them.
rules.why: These keys are case-significant and opaque, so normalizing them would be wrong. Direct verbatim indexing is the convention for such keys.
rules.check: In EF entity/configuration changes, look for opaque Base64Url or similar case-sensitive keys that get a normalized/upper-cased companion column or are compared case-insensitively.
